item.research_question: How can the miscibility gap in bimetallic Co-Mo alloys be overcome to create tunable, highly active catalysts for ammonia decomposition using earth-abundant elements?
item.material_system: Quinary CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (general composition CoxMoyFe10Ni10Cu10 where x + y = 70) and control samples of bimetallic Co-Mo and monometallic Ru
item.processing_route: Carbothermal shock technique involving flash heating and cooling of metal precursors on oxygenated carbon nanofibers; temperature reached 2000–2300 K with ramping rates on the order of 10^5 K s−1 and shock duration of ~55 ms
item.test_conditions: Ammonia decomposition in a plug flow reactor at 250–600 °C using 5 vol% NH3 (and 100 vol% NH3 for specific tests) at a gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) of 36 L gcat−1 h−1
key_findings: HEA-Co25Mo45 achieved a mass-specific reaction rate of 22.1 gNH3 gmetals−1 h−1 at 500 °C, representing an improvement factor of ~19 versus bimetallic Co-Mo and ~3 versus Ru.
The most active catalyst, HEA-Co25Mo45, reached 50% NH3 conversion (T50) at 422 °C, compared to 600 °C for Ru and 600 °C for bimetallic Co-Mo.
The apparent activation energy (Eapp) varied from 64.7 kJ mol−1 for the most active HEA-Co25Mo45 to 123.1 kJ mol−1 for the least active HEA-Co55Mo15.
Nitrogen desorption energy (ΔEN) for HEA-Co25Mo45 was ~79 kJ mol−1, which is very close to the value for Ru (84 kJ mol−1).
Catalytic activity exhibited a volcano-type behavior with respect to nitrogen adsorption energy, peaking at an optimal ΔEN of ~79 kJ mol−1.
The HEA-Co25Mo45 catalyst showed negligible degradation after ~50 hours of continuous operation at 500 °C.
For pure NH3 decomposition, HEA-Co55Mo15 achieved an improvement factor of ~118 versus bimetallic Co-Mo and ~40 versus Ru.
Atomistic modeling confirmed a single solid-solution phase with δ = 5.4% and ΔHmix = 0.65 kJ mol−1, showing no phase segregation up to 1000 K.
item.mechanism: The high catalytic activity is attributed to the robust tuning of surface nitrogen binding strength via the Co/Mo ratio; the optimal activity arises from a tradeoff where Co-rich catalysts bind N too weakly (limiting dehydrogenation) and Mo-rich catalysts bind N too strongly (limiting N2 desorption), with the HEA composition allowing access to the optimal intermediate binding energy (~79 kJ mol−1) predicted by the Sabatier principle.
item.limitations: The text notes that the peak intensities in XRD patterns are low due to the much smaller particle sizes compared to previously reported HEAs, and that the bimetallic Co-Mo catalysts are constrained by large miscibility gaps in their phase diagram.
item.future_work: The authors propose designing practical reactors with cascaded catalyst layers having gradually changing nitrogen binding strengths to match the varying concentration of NH3 along the flow, which can be readily achieved by varying the Co/Mo ratios in HEA catalysts.
quotes: Quinary CoMoFeNiCu nanoparticles are synthesized in a single solid-solution phase with robust control over the Co/Mo atomic ratio, including those ratios considered to be immiscible according to the Co-Mo bimetallic phase diagram.
The finding here can be further correlated to the dependence of reaction orders on ΔEN.
